title: Declare the four cockpit-vocabulary herding shapes the dispatcher already serves
action:
THE RED, already diagnosed. `cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test registry_dispatch` fails at registry_dispatch.rs:393: 'the dispatcher serves these shapes and the registry does not declare them, so `bee --help --all` reports them as unknown commands' -- naming `bee herding agent-start`, `bee herding pane`, `bee herding pane-id`, `bee herding result`. The test derives `served` by scanning the match arms of `pub fn try_native` in src/herding.rs (:122-139, where all four are wired to pane_verbs::) and compares against every `commands[].invoke` in src/generated/registry_payload.json. Red at origin/main since the tmux-herding-cockpit work landed; it stayed invisible because cargo test stops at the first failing target and two earlier reds masked it.

THE DECISION IS ALREADY MADE -- these are COMMANDS, not internal plumbing, so they get declared. Evidence, do not re-litigate it: pane_verbs.rs opens by naming itself 'the transport-neutral cockpit vocabulary (tmux-herding-cockpit D2)' and states 'a cockpit role document and bootstrap-cockpit.sh act on panes ONLY through these verbs -- never a raw `herdr` or `tmux` line. A cold control agent then reads ONE vocabulary, whatever `herding.transport` names.' They are the transport-neutral twins of `herding herdr-result` and `herding herdr-pane-id`, BOTH of which are already declared in the registry. src/router.rs:100-105 already lists all four in PORTED under the comment 'tmux-herding-cockpit D2 -- the transport-neutral cockpit vocabulary'; only the registry was missed. Do NOT add anything to NOT_A_COMMAND_SURFACE (registry_dispatch.rs:321) -- it excludes whole namespaces, herding is a real command surface, and excluding it would hide every herding verb.

THE WORK. Add exactly four entries to the `commands` array of packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/generated/registry_payload.json, named `herding.agent-start`, `herding.pane`, `herding.pane-id`, `herding.result`, each matching the shape the file's existing herding entries already use (see herding.herdr-pane-id and herding.run as the closest templates): `name`, `invoke`, `description`, `parameters` (JSON-Schema object with `properties` and `required`), and `examples`. Place them beside the other herding entries, keeping the file's existing ordering convention. Write each `description` from the REAL behaviour in src/herding/pane_verbs.rs -- the verb list for `pane` is current|list|split|run|send-text|read|rename|close|layout|tab-create|tab-list|tab-focus; `agent-start <job> --kind <k> --pane <id> -- <args...>`; `pane-id --label <label>`; `result <dotted.path>` reads one `{ok,transport,result}` envelope on stdin and prints `result.<path>`, sharing herdr-result's own reader so the two cannot drift. Every verb prints exactly one JSON envelope: {"ok":true,"transport":"herdr|tmux","result":{...}} exit 0, or {"ok":false,...,"error":{...}} exit 1. Do not invent flags -- read them off the argument parsing in pane_verbs.rs.

EXAMPLES ARE EXECUTED, so get them right. registry_dispatch.rs:19-27 and :143-152 state the contract: every entry carries `examples[0]`, the test RUNS it in a sandbox cwd, and an entry with NO `unavailable` marker must not be refused, while an entry WITH one must hit the unavailable path. Follow `herding.herdr-pane-id` (`bee herding herdr-pane-id --label x`) and `herding.run` (`bee herding run --dry-run ... --main-root . --json`) -- both run clean today. Pick the cheapest side-effect-free invocation for each of the four and VERIFY each one by hand before you commit. If a verb genuinely cannot run without a live tmux or herdr transport, give that entry an `unavailable` marker in the same shape herding.enable and herding.disable already use ({reason, fix}) rather than inventing a new mechanism or weakening the test -- and say on the cap which of the four you marked and why.

Do NOT edit registry_dispatch.rs, herding.rs, pane_verbs.rs, or router.rs. The registry is the only thing missing.

Also run `bee dev release-manifest --check` before you cap: the payload is compiled into the binary, so confirm nothing else drifted.
verify: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test registry_dispatch --test registry_contracts --test front_door

truths: All four entries carry an examples[0] that the registry suite actually executes without an unknown-command refusal, or an unavailable marker in the existing {reason, fix} shape
registry_contracts and front_door are green -- the embedded payload's shape and freshness pins still hold
No test file, dispatcher, or router source was edited; only the registry payload changed
The full declared suite is green

trace.outcome: Declared herding pane/agent-start/pane-id/result in the command registry, clearing the dispatcher-vs-registry red
deviations: Edited packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/catalog.rs, one file beyond the cell's declared list (reserved under hrg-w1 first). Declaring the four entries grew the registry's distinct flag vocabulary 181->188, which fails catalog::tests::distinct_flag_vocabulary_is_pinned_so_growth_is_a_decision — a unit test masked by the same first-failing-target effect that hid the cell's own red. That test's own message prescribes the remedy (bump PINNED_FLAG_COUNT and say why), and the cell's must-haves require the full declared suite green, so this is fix-blocking-breakage, not scope creep. catalog.rs is not on the cell's do-not-edit list.

No entry took an `unavailable` marker. The cell offered one as a fallback for a verb needing a live transport, but that fallback cannot apply here: registry_dispatch asserts the OTHER direction too — a marked entry MUST hit the `bee: not built into this binary` refusal, and all four verbs are built, so a marker would have failed as `marked_but_alive`. Instead each example is side-effect-free by construction and was run by hand against a live herdr transport before commit.

Recorded for the next reader: the four verbs never emit a router-level refusal at all — they print their own {ok:false,...} envelope — so the registry-dispatch walk cannot detect a wrong example for them. Example safety here rests on the hand-run check, not on the suite.
